title: Crane Over The Head
description: A crane over the head rises on the arm until the camera looks nearly straight down, a person becoming a map. The end state is overhead, not a high three-quarter.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Finish by looking down. A body on a floor, a crime, a dance, a figure lost in pattern: the arm climbs and continues until the lens is almost nadir.
A crane-up that eases back into a skyline is a different end: the person becomes geography from an oblique height. Overhead and bird's-eye can be locked.
This shot is the travel that arrives there.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Jib or Technocrane, start at human height or a three-quarter, boom up and over until tilt is nearly 90 degrees down. A little boom-out keeps the subject from sliding off.
Prompt: Crane over the head of [Subject], the arm rising until the camera looks nearly straight down, a person becoming a map.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to end on a downward map of a person. Do not stop at a high three-quarter and call it over the head.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Crane Over travels the arm over an obstacle or crowd without requiring nadir. Overhead Top-Down is the locked top-down frame.
Bird's-Eye View is the high downward view as a size. Crane-over-the-head is the boom that becomes those views.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Untouchables uses high downward cranes (the station, the pram, the floor as a map). Birdman booms over theater space until people become pattern.
Grammar: rise until you look down.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a crane-up that stays oblique, or a locked overhead with no travel. The tell: we never look down, or we were already down.
The fix: boom up and over until the lens is nearly straight down.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Crane Over The Head in film?
A crane over the head booms up and over a person until the camera looks nearly straight down. The person becomes a map.
Crane Over The Head vs Overhead Top-Down
Overhead is the locked top-down frame. Crane over the head is the travel that arrives there from a human starting height.
When should I use Crane Over The Head?
Use it to finish by looking down on a person. Do not stop at a high three-quarter.
How do I prompt Crane Over The Head for AI image or video?
Write a boom that ends almost straight down. Example: Crane over the head of [Subject], the arm rising until the camera looks nearly straight down, a person becoming a map.
